lessons: Start with striking comparative anchors or bold historic/scale facts ('older than the United States', 'tuna vs cod look like different animals') to push initial retention above 1.2-1.8.
Eliminate filler setup lines and stating the obvious (e.g., 'They look like similar fruits' or 'They are not just there to look cool'); these cause massive immediate drops between 28% and 33%.
Avoid middle-of-video pauses and explicit countdown prompts (e.g., 'Pause and guess... three, two, one'), as they create predictable drop-offs rather than engagement.
Frame scientific explanations around active visual contrast rather than abstract mental exercises ('think about what happens when...'), which severely hurt mid-to-end retention.
worst_moment_types: Obvious statements and filler commentary ('They are not just there to look cool', 'They look like similar fruits').
Mid-script interactive pauses and countdowns ('Pause and guess... three, two, one').
Abstract thought prompts and passive rhetorical setups ('Now think about what happens when...').
best_hook_types: Extreme comparative anchors comparing subject to surprising benchmarks ('older than the United States').
Direct sensory/visual paradoxes between two familiar objects ('bluefin tuna and cod look like two completely different animals').
Subversion of widespread scientific assumptions ('Pluto seemed like our edge, yet Kuiper Belt extends much further').
